newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BOJ comments fails to excite SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs.
newsitem.headline: BOJ comments fails to excite SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita's comments on Wednesday failed to ignite any reaction from the short-term Japanese rates, leaving SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures unscathed.

"There was nothing new in what Matsushita said," said a Japanese dealer. "What dominated the markets today is the very strong dollar and the weak yen." The yen hit a 46-month low of 118.75 to the dollar on worries about health of Japanese banks.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's suggestion that there were no immediate plans to hike rates on Tuesday fuelled the dollar against most major currencies.
In a press conference, Matsushita indicated no shift in the BOJ's near-term steady rate policy. His comments that the Japanese economy was enroute to a moderate recovery were also taken in stride.

Euroyen was locked within a narrow three-tick range by a stronger Japanese stock market and a weaker Japanese yen against the U.S. dollar, dealers said. September Euroyen was at 99.31 at 1130 GMT, unchanged from its IMM close at 99.31. Turnover was around 4,700 lots. September Euroyen was expected to stay range-bound within 99.28-99.32 this week, with a potential upward bias despite the weaker yen.
Japanese government bond (JGB) futures settled at 126.20 against their opening 126.04.
"JGBs came down in the late afternoon after London opened due to the weaker yen rather than anything else," another dealer said.

June Eurodollar futures finished scarcely changed at 94.21 against the IMM close at 94.22. Dealers said the market was likely to stay range-bound within 94.15-94.25 this week as no U.S. rate hikes were expected from the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in February. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
